classification.question_topic: Whether anyone else has seen a stark white/pearlescent, fog-ceiling library with repeating chest-height shelves

position.relative_to: repeating sets of shelves going on for a while in all directions except for the way I came in

qualities.raw_description: Library space is 'all stark white and sort of pearlescent' (except books). Shelves are about chest height. Space is 'so flat' that repeating sets of shelves extend 'for a while in all directions' except the entry direction. 'No visible ceiling', only 'a mixture of white and blue fog fading and shifting into itself.' Felt 'more ethereal-feeling.' Dream was 'so vivid' and 'felt more real than waking life.'

boundaries.description: No visible ceiling; ceiling area is a mixture of white and blue fog fading and shifting into itself.
Shelves repeat for a while in all directions; only exception noted is 'except for the way I came in' (entry direction differs from repeating layout).

interactions.description: Dreamer enters the library area; observes repeating shelf sets extending in most directions and fog ceiling.

Dreamer notes shelves are chest height; environment is stark white/pearlescent; books are realistic old hardcovers in various conditions and colors; ceiling not visible due to shifting white-blue fog.

extraction.extraction_notes: Image appears to be a hand-drawn sketch of the described library: low shelves with books and triangular/architectural shapes; handwritten notes include 'shifting pattern' and 'shifting decoration not fire' (text partially legible). Narrative does not specify people/entities, lighting source, or exact entry structure beyond 'the way I came in.'
